# Draft:7th General Assembly of Prince Edward Island

}}
The 5th General Assembly of the Island of St. John  began in 1802 and lasted until 1806. This period was a significant turning point in the colony’s legal and social history, as it transitioned through a decade of legislative inactivity and faced major immigration milestones.
The Assembly sat at the pleasure of the Governor of St. John's Island, Edmund Fanning until he was succeeded by Joseph Frederick Wallet DesBarres in 1804.
In 1803, the Assembly considered critical legislation regarding delinquent quitrents. This was part of a broader effort to revest lands in the Crown that had been granted to absentee landlords who failed to fulfill settlement conditions. On April 2, 1803, Governor Fanning signed an act that established a procedure for investigating whether grant conditions were met, a key step in the ongoing "Land Question".
James Curtis was chosen as speaker.
